authors: Carl R. Russell and Jaewoo Jung and Gina Willink and Brett Glasner
title: Wind Tunnel and Hover Performance Test Results for Multicopter UAS Vehicles
reviewed_location: NASA record abstract and NASA Multicopter UAS Performance Test project description; full PDF download was unavailable in this session
evidence_type: Primary wind-tunnel test report; abstract-level evidence used
supports: Five multicopters were tested for forces, moments and electrical power while varying wind speed, rotor speed and attitude.
boundary: Supports measuring aerodynamic and electrical responses, not a Tello formation ranking or a conversion from fan level to metres per second.

authors: Bart Theys and Joris De Schutter
title: Forward flight tests of a quadcopter unmanned aerial vehicle with various spherical body diameters
venue: International Journal of Micro Air Vehicles, 12
reviewed_location: Test procedure and data processing; Power consumption in forward flight; Conclusion
evidence_type: Primary single-quadcopter flight experiment, full text
supports: Power first decreased from hover and then increased with speed; motor-speed corrections also produced power fluctuations during nominal steady flight.
boundary: Larger aircraft and much faster flight than the present 0.1 m/s segment; neither the optimal speed nor fluctuation magnitude transfers to Tello.

authors: Diana A. Olejnik and Sunyi Wang and Julien Dupeyroux and Stein Stroobants and Matěj Karásek and Christophe De Wagter and Guido de Croon
title: An Experimental Study of Wind Resistance and Power Consumption in MAVs with a Low-Speed Multi-Fan Wind System
reviewed_location: Sections II-B (flow characterisation), IV-A (steady wind), IV-B (gusts), V
evidence_type: Primary experimental author preprint, full text
supports: The Crazyflie quadrotor had relatively constant power across the tested wind speeds; the authors mapped the fan-array flow spatially.
boundary: Not Tello, not five-drone formations, and not evidence that the present fan field is uniform or nonuniform. The present wind levels remain categorical.

authors: Karan P. Jain and Trey Fortmuller and Jaeseung Byun and Simo A. Mäkiharju and Mark W. Mueller
title: Modeling of aerodynamic disturbances for proximity flight of multirotors
venue: IEEE International Conference on Unmanned Aircraft Systems
reviewed_location: Sections II, IV and V, particularly the separation-dependent disturbance results
evidence_type: Primary two-quadcopter experiments and model, full text
supports: Relative horizontal and vertical separation affects induced forces and torques; inflow-related thrust changes were more important than frame drag in the studied setup.
boundary: Mainly upper/lower-vehicle downwash, with model validity restricted by separation. It does not establish that coplanar 75 cm always beats 50 cm.

authors: Guanya Shi and Wolfgang Hönig and Yisong Yue and Soon-Jo Chung
title: Neural-Swarm: Decentralized Close-Proximity Multirotor Control Using Learned Interactions
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation; author version arXiv:2003.02992
reviewed_location: Sections V-A, V-C and V-D: battery-aware calibration, swapping experiments and interaction fields
evidence_type: Primary multi-quadcopter control experiments, full text
supports: Measured multi-vehicle interactions depend on relative position and velocity and are not a simple sum of pairwise effects; battery voltage was included in thrust calibration.
boundary: Mostly vertically offset swapping, with a height-tracking objective; not a measured energy ranking of the present five coplanar formations.

authors: C. Christian Wolf and Daniel Schanz and Clemens Schwarz and Alexander Heintz and Johannes Bosbach and Tobias Strübing and Andreas Schröder
title: Volumetric wake investigation of a free-flying quadcopter using Shake-The-Box Lagrangian particle tracking
reviewed_location: Sections 3.2–3.4 and Conclusion: hover, ground interaction and forward-flight wake
evidence_type: Primary time-resolved 3D flow measurements, full text
supports: A quadcopter wake is spatially structured and changes between hover, ground-effect and forward-flight cases; forward-flight wakes become skewed.
boundary: One 0.5 m-span quadcopter, including 3.1 m/s forward flight; not a direct observation of neighbouring Tello interactions at 50/75 cm.

title: Formation-based Selection of Drone Swarm Services
reviewed_location: Sections 4.1 and 5.1; Tables 2 and 3; experimental variables
supports: Formation rankings changed when the study added wake-related contributions to drag; the framework distinguishes position-dependent consumption under different winds.
boundary: Phantom 3 simulation with 15.6 m/s flight, not this Tello telemetry. Tailwind was excluded. P=F_D v is drag-related power, not the entire hover electrical power. Do not import its winning formations.

authors: Xijing Liu and Kevin Lam and Balsam Alkouz and Babar Shahzaad and Athman Bouguettaya
title: Constraint-based Formation of Drone Swarms
reviewed_location: Section II: five-Tello indoor demonstration, routing, formation and recharging constraints
supports: A five-Tello indoor system uses mission pads and adapts formations within a delivery framework with wind and charging constraints.
boundary: Useful architectural precedent, not independent experimental validation of the present rate table or charging model.

authors: Amir Mirzaeinia and Mostafa Hassanalian and Kooktae Lee and Mehdi Mirzaeinia
title: Energy conservation of V-shaped swarming fixed-wing drones through position reconfiguration
evidence_type: Primary fixed-wing theoretical study; abstract and introduction reviewed
supports: The studied energy-balancing and V-formation mechanism concerns fixed-wing aircraft.
boundary: A contrast source: its savings, optimal geometry and leader burden cannot be assumed for hovering or slow-moving quadcopters.

authors: Anna A. Kostek and Johannes N. Braukmann and Felix Lößle and Sebastian Miesner and Antonio Visingardi and Ronan Boisard and Vasilis Riziotis and Manuel Keßler and Anthony D. Gardner
title: Experimental and Computational Investigation of Aerodynamic Interactions in Quadrotor Configurations
venue: Journal of the American Helicopter Society, 69, 022009
reviewed_location: Experimental setup; two-rotor tandem and oblique results; rotor-efficiency discussion; conclusions (pp. 2, 6–7, 14–16)
evidence_type: Primary wind-tunnel thrust measurements, power-derived torque, PIV and computational comparison
supports: Wake-core downwash reduced downstream thrust; lateral offsets changed the inflow and could improve thrust per power. Rotor loading connects wake geometry to RPM requirements.
boundary: Rotor rigs at 12.9 m/s, not five complete Tellos at 50/75 cm. Used for mechanisms, not transferred saving percentages or rankings.
